rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 2 "You described it; something else built it": line 11 "The parts of an agent stay the same: context, a goal, tools, checks, a boundary, a loop." is class (a) doctrine restatement: the very next slide (chunk 3, line 15 include, slides/parts-hold-model-rotates.md) opens "The parts are stable: context, tools, boundary, checks, loop, interface." The parts claim is announced twice in adjacent slides, and the two lists disagree (goal vs interface), so the room sees two different anatomies. Harm = redundant bullet plus a list that contradicts itself across slides; present. Obvious fix does not degrade: slide 2's job per its header is 'you described it, an agent built it', which needs no parts list.

suggestions.now: The parts of an agent stay the same: context, a goal, tools, checks, a boundary, a loop. You decide each one. An agent assembles them from your description.
suggestions.proposed: You decide what the agent knows, what it is after, what it may touch and how it is checked. An agent assembles all of that from your description.

suggestions.now: The parts are stable: context, tools, boundary, checks, loop, interface.
suggestions.proposed: The parts are stable: context, tools, a goal, checks, a boundary, a loop.
